summary: The legacy compatibility repair preserves password-account rights with conservative discovery fallback, optional displayed-owner404 binding, same-owner export guards and actual current-password checks. No material defect was found in those specific request/UI changes. However, independent synthetic reproduction shows expired Apple unlink linkage survives the normal privacy scheduler when auth keys are absent. Its only local expiry caller is gated off with crypto_ready=false. This violates the promised bounded unlink/missing-key erasure and requires a local key-independent cleanup schedule. The prior three e4 authority/native fixes remain intact; this newly verified scheduler path does not restamp prior review results.

findings.title: Missing auth keys disable the only expired-unlink/metadata sweep
findings.trigger: A configured account explicitly removes Apple while remote cleanup is pending, then the service runs without the usable auth keyring. This is the missing-key/unconfigured boundary now exposed by the compatibility repair.
findings.actual_behavior: main.create_app starts the auth dispatcher only when config.modern_auth.crypto_ready. ModernAuthService.dispatch_one is the only production caller of AuthMetadataRepository.cleanup_expired. The independent normal privacy scheduler never calls an auth expiry sweep. At 25h after unlink, actual normal privacy maintenance leaves one unlinked plaintext subject-to-owner binding and one expired cleanup job; explicit auth dispatch immediately erases both.
findings.impact: Disconnected provider linkage and expired cleanup metadata can remain indefinitely beyond the documented 24h erasure bound while the owner/account remains active. The same disabled sweep also owns other short-lived auth metadata expiry. No unauthorized session restoration or production data exposure was demonstrated.
findings.evidence_kind: Independently exercised production unlink/SQLite/normal privacy sweep with synthetic fixtures and clock; startup crypto gate independently inspected statically. No full app restart or device/live-provider execution claimed.
findings.reproduction_command: Run the supplied script with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 /workspace/brain_buddy-auth/backend/.venv/bin/python from the exact review worktree backend directory.
findings.reproduction_script:
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from datetime import timedelta
import pytest
from tests import conftest
from tests.test_modern_auth_apple_integration import apple_runtime
from tests.test_modern_auth_unlink_authority import owner_with_binding, remove
from app.core.config import ModernAuthSettings
from app.main import _run_privacy_maintenance_sweep

with TemporaryDirectory(prefix='modern-auth-deac-missing-key-retention-') as directory:
    data=Path(directory)/'data'; data.mkdir()
    mp=pytest.MonkeyPatch()
    fixture=conftest.container.__wrapped__(data,mp)
    container=next(fixture)
    try:
        service, _, _, provider, clock=apple_runtime.__wrapped__(container)
        container.modern_auth_service=service
        owner, token=owner_with_binding(service,provider,clock)
        remove(service,owner,token,'apple')
        clock.now += timedelta(hours=25)
        service.settings=ModernAuthSettings()
        service.box=None
        service.apple.secret_box=None
        def counts():
            with service.store.connection() as connection:
                row=connection.execute('SELECT state,payload_json FROM auth_identity_bindings').fetchone()
                return {'bindings':connection.execute('SELECT count(*) FROM auth_identity_bindings').fetchone()[0],
                        'jobs':connection.execute('SELECT count(*) FROM auth_apple_cleanup_jobs').fetchone()[0],
                        'state':None if row is None else row['state']}
        assert service.settings.crypto_ready is False
        before=counts()
        assert before['state']=='unlinked' and before['jobs']==1
        _run_privacy_maintenance_sweep(container)
        after_privacy=counts()
        assert after_privacy==before
        service.dispatch_one()
        after_auth=counts()
        assert after_auth=={'bindings':0,'jobs':0,'state':None}
        print({'crypto_ready':False,'elapsed_hours':25,
               'before_normal_privacy_maintenance':before,
               'after_normal_privacy_maintenance':after_privacy,
               'positive_control_explicit_auth_dispatch':after_auth})
    finally:
        try:next(fixture)
        except StopIteration:pass
        mp.undo()
findings.required_correction: Ensure existing local auth expiry/settled-unlink erasure is scheduled even with missing/unusable auth keys. Keep provider network operations availability-gated and preserve active cleanup lease/generation safety; do not extend retention or account-purge deadlines.

inspected_boundaries: Complete product diff from 1f4, all 221 lines of LegacyAccountActions, all 315 lines of its tests and additional real-HTTP/discovery/export guard tests inspected.

Legacy fallback requires no load error, a password-bearing account, successful discovery with web_account_origin=null and all optional methods false. Passwordless and failed-discovery paths do not render legacy controls.
Connected method metadata remains visible; a failed availability load yields retry instead of rewriting bindings or choosing the legacy mode.

All compatible account route functions depend on get_account_user; a mismatched optional X-BrainBuddy-Expected-Owner raises generic 404 before account read/export/mutation. Headerless legacy Mac/password wire meanings remain unchanged.

Password/delete/export frontend paths bind the captured displayed owner. Export checks local owner before fetch and after await blob before any object URL/anchor download. AuthStore's cleanup generation check prevents clearing a replacement session.

Password/delete/export refs block overlapping submissions within each action;44 CSS-pixel minimum/control focus styling retained. Existing backend password rechecks, last-method/operator/modern proof endpoints are unchanged.
Discovery origin now requires validated origins and usable keyring; prior provider/email flags remain controlled by the same ready/configuration rules.
Nginx removes only its 32-hex X-Request-ID injection; absent client header lets existing middleware generate canonical UUID. Header validation/CRT behavior otherwise unchanged.

Legacy E2E outcome/negative cases remain strict; account tests return to the original Password/Data/DangerZone outcomes, and login/signup helpers only explicitly select their methods while preserving deep-link state.
No schema, floor, vendored A2A, Mac product, or native callback/finalizer change was found.
